stories.title: Is AI 'one big bubble'? Behind the tech sell-off
stories.summary: Investors are selling off AI-related stocks as doubts are starting to surface over whether the massive spending on AI is worth the investment and whether it's "one big bubble."

stories.title: Senate passes war powers resolution, Tim Kaine says there's more work to be done
stories.summary: The Senate has voted to take away President Trump's power to wage war with Iran. NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Virginia Democrat Tim Kaine, a sponsor of the bill.

stories.title: Efforts to protect gorillas from Ebola in the DRC
stories.summary: The staff of a wildlife preserve in the Democratic Republic of Congo are trying desperately to keep their gorillas from exposure to Ebola. Gorillas can get it and almost all of them die from it.

stories.title: Fraught state fair opens on the National Mall
stories.summary: The Great American State Fair begins in D.C. as part of the country's 250th anniversary celebrations. It's bringing hundreds of exhibits to the National Mall, though some state aren't participating.

stories.title: Red Cross volunteers work to combat heat-related deaths at Phoenix mobile homes
stories.summary: In Phoenix, Arizona, a disproportionate number of indoor heat-related deaths happen in mobile homes. Red Cross volunteers are working to change that.

stories.title: A Revolutionary War soldier's DNA links him to living relatives
stories.summary: Continental Army soldier John Pumphrey enlisted as a teenager in 1777 and fought at significant battles before his death in action against the British in Camden, S.C.
